$doc: The stack profile. Every path, package and command in this kit is read from here. Run /adapt to refresh it after a framework upgrade or a move. Reference: obsidian/architecture/stack-profile.md
notes: Styling is styled-components, not a CSS token file. The design tokens are TypeScript: src/styles/colors.ts declares the literal palette (_colors) and toVars() turns it into var(--color-*) references that printVars() emits into :root inside src/styles/index.ts. That is a two-tier system (primitive -> CSS var), not the kit's three-tier convention, so conventions.tokenTiers is false. See ADR-0101.

Responsive sizing goes through the SmartCSSGrid helpers rm()/em()/media from src/styles (src/styles/grid/grid.tsx), which scale px values against a 1920/1440/768/576 grid. A raw px in a styled-component is usually a bug; use rm().
paths.assets is null on purpose: content assets are served from Strapi through the API layer, and public/ holds only 3D models, textures, fonts, favicons/PWA icons and OG images.

paths.env is null: there is no validated env module yet. 52 process.env reads are scattered across src, so verify.sh will FAIL the env check until one exists. This is known debt, not a mis-detection. See ADR-0104.

The code reads NEXT_PUBLIC_BASEURL (no underscore between BASE and URL) in 10 places while .env declares NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL. Only src/utils/strapi.ts reads the underscored name. Every canonical URL, sitemap entry and OG tag is therefore falling through to the hardcoded 'https://www.streetbarbell.com' literal.

paths.protected covers the two vendored engines from the next14-starter: src/components/Text (TextEngine 1381 lines, TextProgress 834 lines, TLine) and src/components/Springs (Spring, Inview, SpringTrigger, Hover, Handle, ProgressTrigger). Consume and wrap them; do not edit them without sign-off.

There is no single shared rAF ticker. src/hooks/useLoop.ts starts one requestAnimationFrame per subscriber and src/layouts/ScrollLayout drives Lenis on its own loop. This deviates from the kit's one-loop rule (ADR-0005). See ADR-0103.

i18n is next-intl with locale-prefixed routes under src/app/[locale]. The locale list has three sources that must agree: src/config/locales.ts (static, used by middleware and Edge), NEXT_PUBLIC_LOCALES, and Strapi via src/utils/locales.ts.
commands.typecheck is not a package.json script; tsc runs through npx. There is no test command.

commands.start is NOT `yarn start`: next.config.mjs sets output:'standalone', and Next refuses to run `next start` against it. A local production run needs `yarn build`, then `cp -R public .next/standalone/public`, `cp -R .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static`, then `cd .next/standalone && node server.js`. Verified 2026-09-17.

next.config.mjs config trap: never put a package that a client component's import graph can reach into experimental.serverComponentsExternalPackages. An ESM package externalised there (axios 1.11 was) makes every importer an async webpack module, and an async client reference resolves to undefined in Next 14.2's SSR flight client — every page 500s with 'Element type is invalid' and nothing in the message names the config. See ADR-0106.

The Draco decoder is vendored at public/draco/ (from three/examples/jsm/libs/draco/gltf) and reached through DRACO_DECODER_PATH in src/utils/dracoDecoder.ts. Refresh it when three is upgraded. See ADR-0108.

Media loading: every media slot must show a placeholder from the first paint. Use MediaComponent for CMS media (it owns one), or Skeleton/PlaceholderImage as a drop-in wherever a bare next/image would go - never a bare next/image for content imagery. Pass sizes, or a fill image asks the optimiser for the largest device width, and priority above the fold; placeholderTone='dark' only for slots over dark art. A video poster goes through next/image, never the <video poster> attribute, which is not optimisable. images.minimumCacheTTL in next.config.mjs is deliberately 1 day: long enough to stop 5-minute re-encodes, short enough that a 'Replace media' (same URL) shows within a day - never make media caches long or immutable. See ADR-0110, ADR-0118.

The loader curtain gates on HERO media and HERO scenes only, via useRequireMedia and useRequireScene. It never gates on a scene a client cannot render (canRenderWebGL) or on a below-the-fold scene - home's globe prewarms in the background instead. Getting that wrong cost four page types their entire Lighthouse performance score, because a curtain that never lifts means no Largest Contentful Paint. See ADR-0111.

useWindowWidth() returns 0 on the SERVER. Any MARKUP that branches on width must be gated with useMounted(), desktop as the server assumption: {(!mounted || width > 768) && <Desktop/>} and {mounted && width <= 768 && <Mobile/>}. Getting this wrong made every page of the site fail hydration (React #418/#423). Props and numbers do not need the guard - only DOM shape. See ADR-0114.

Touch behaviour is decided by useTouchDevice() - (hover: none) and (pointer: coarse) - never by viewport width, so a narrow window on a laptop keeps mouse interaction. The 3D configurators use it for the two-finger gesture rules and the auto-rotate. See ADR-0114.

Failure states are designed, never blank: src/app/[locale]/error.tsx (branded, keeps the shell) and src/app/global-error.tsx (self-contained) both read NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL - it is NOT set yet and falls back to a guessed address. A failed map or media slot holds its space in colors.mediaPlaceholder. See ADR-0112.

Never gate behaviour on WHO is asking. isBot() matches the user agent only; checking navigator.webdriver silently stripped the hero scene from every automation-controlled browser, including the screenshot harness. Use canRenderWebGL() - capability, not identity. See ADR-0113.

Media slowness is the ORIGIN, not the app (measured 2026-09-18): the Strapi host costs ~0.7s of latency per request before any payload (470ms of that is TLS), serves 8MB originals at ~2.5MB/s, sends Cache-Control: max-age=300 on uploads (whose URLs are NOT immutable - Replace media keeps them; 1-day fix pending in the Strapi repo, ADR-0118), has no CDN, and generates only a 245px thumbnail for a 2940px source. App-side mitigation is already in place; the rest is server config.

Performance baseline 2026-09-18, production build, warm image cache. Desktop Lighthouse: perf 78-93, SEO 100, CLS 0, LCP <=2.5s on every page type. Mobile: perf 47-74, LCP 5.5-9.1s - bound by JavaScript (bootup-time 6.0s at 4x CPU), NOT by the loader curtain, which was measured and ruled out. Harness in the session scratchpad: perf/lh.mjs. See ADR-0111.

Nothing may fetch on mount what the server already rendered: Header and Footer receive initialData from src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx, and anything a closed panel needs (the header mega-menus) goes through src/utils/onIdle.ts. See ADR-0110.

The globe's surface maps are 2048x2048 webp in public/models/textures/ (earth_{diffuse,normal,roughness,night}_2k.webp), loaded with useTexture. low_res_earth.glb is still fetched but for its GEOMETRY only - its own 6000x6000 maps are replaced before the first draw. high_res_earth.glb (11.2MB) and earth_lights.glb are kept in public/models/ as source art and are NOT fetched at runtime. Check texture dimensions, not file size: the old set was 8000-10000px square, ~1.4GB of VRAM and ~3.4s to upload. See ADR-0109.
Both globes render one component, src/views/DistributionView/components/PlanetModel.tsx - HomeView's Composition imports it from there. Nothing in it may assume which page it is on.

3D scene performance: src/utils/deviceTier.ts owns per-tier DPR and renderer flags (read once at construction), src/utils/warmupScene.ts owns the prewarm, and the loader curtain in src/layouts/AssetsLoaderLayout/Loader.tsx waits for every scene a view registered with useRequireScene. See ADR-0107.

Both yarn.lock and package-lock.json are committed. yarn.lock is the one that is actually maintained (last touched 2025-09-03 vs 2025-08-26) and the README documents yarn. Treat package-lock.json as stale.
